title: Purple Suits for Diwali 2026: Plum vs Violet – Which One Is You?
excerpt: Purple is the festive colour of 2026. How to choose between a regal plum suit and a twirl-ready violet Nyra cut – with styling, jewellery and fit tips.
body:
Purple has quietly become the festive colour of the season. It feels royal like maroon, fresher than red, and it glows in diya light – which is exactly why we see it at every Diwali party from Jaipur to New Jersey. If you are planning your Diwali 2026 outfit (Diwali falls on **8 November**), here is a simple guide to two purple suits from our Jaipur studio – and how to make either one look its best.

## Why purple works so well for Diwali

- **It flatters every skin tone.** Deep plum warms up wheatish and dusky skin; brighter violet makes fair and olive skin glow.
- **It photographs beautifully.** Purple holds its colour in warm lamp light and in flash photos, without turning dull.
- **It is festive without being bridal.** You look dressed up, but you will not compete with the bride at a family function.

## Plum: rich, calm and elegant

Our [plum purple embroidered cotton suit](/products/plum-purple-embroidered-cotton-3-piece-suit/) is the classic choice. Large pink roses and sage-green leaves frame the neckline, tiny embroidered buttis are scattered over the body, and the pants have an embroidered floral hem. The soft cotton dupatta keeps the look graceful.

**Wear it to:** Lakshmi puja, Karva Chauth, family dinners, office Diwali celebrations.

**Jewellery:** oxidised silver jhumkas, a slim kada and a small potli bag.

**Shoes:** block heels or gold juttis.

## Violet: flowy, fun and twirl-ready

Our [violet Nyra cut sequin suit](/products/violet-nyra-cut-sequin-embroidered-cotton-3-piece-suit/) is made for movement. The Nyra cut – a fitted yoke gathered into an A-line flare – sways when you walk and twirls when you dance. The yoke is embroidered in tonal thread with tiny sequins, and bandhani-style print panels add a Rajasthani touch.

**Wear it to:** Diwali card parties, garba nights, mehendi, festive lunches.

**Jewellery:** long silver jhumkas or chandbalis; keep the neck bare.

**Shoes:** juttis for dancing, clear heels for photos.

## Plum or violet? A quick guide

| If you… | Choose |
|---|---|
| Love classic, graceful looks | Plum |
| Want a flowy, twirly silhouette | Violet |
| Have a puja or formal family event | Plum |
| Have a party, garba or mehendi | Violet |
| Prefer a straight, structured fit | Plum |
| Want an easy, forgiving flare | Violet |

## Festive does not have to mean heavy

Both suits are **100% cotton**. That means you stay comfortable from the morning puja to late-night celebrations – and you can wash and wear them again for Navratri, Eid, Holi and weddings all year round. In a heated home in Toronto or London, cotton is far more comfortable than heavy synthetic festive wear.

## Getting the fit right when you shop from abroad

Buying Indian clothes online from the USA, UK or Canada can feel like a gamble on size. We make it simple:

1. Use the **Fit Finder** on any product page – enter bust, waist and hip and it recommends your size.
2. Or send us your measurements and we will **stitch the suit to fit you** at no extra cost.
3. We send you photos of your piece being made in Jaipur before it ships.

## Frequently asked questions

**When should I order for Diwali delivery abroad?**
Order at least 2–3 weeks before Diwali. Custom-fit pieces take 5–7 working days to make, plus 5–10 business days for express delivery.

**Will the purple colour fade?**
Wash separately in cold water the first few times and dry in shade – the colour will stay rich for many seasons.

**Can I wear these suits after Diwali?**
Absolutely. Plum is lovely for winter weddings and office events; violet is perfect for Navratri, mehendi and summer functions.
